author: blu
body: THE ANSWER IS A VARIANT, NOT AN INTEGER. An evaluator that returns 0 for a name it does not know is indistinguishable from one that read a zero, and in a debugger that means dumping the wrong page and believing it. Every failure says what it failed on and where.

author: blu
body: WHAT THIS IS NOT. No parentheses, no unary minus, no function calls. This is an address calculator for a command line: the shape it must cover is a literal or a name, then operators and more of the same. The design specifies exactly that set and nothing about grouping, and inventing grouping would be building for a need nobody has stated.

author: blu
body: A parse step: what was produced, and how far the scanner got. The index is what lets the caller tell "the expression ended here" from "there is trailing rubbish", which is the difference between `0x10` and `0x10 )`.

author: blu
body: The addresses a person actually types at a bare-metal debugger, taken from `docs/ArchitectsSketchbook.md` rather than invented. A name that is silently wrong here is worse than a name that is absent, so the list is short and every entry is one this system genuinely uses.

author: blu
body: That is the same CCE assumption this project has shipped repeatedly, and it survived being written by someone who had spent the same day writing a chapter warning about it. A table is the only form that cannot be wrong about an ordering it does not assume.

author: blu
body: Both number scanners carry a digit COUNT, so `0x` with nothing after it is an error rather than zero. A literal that silently becomes zero is the same class of lie as an unknown name that becomes zero.

author: blu
body: The trailing check is what makes `0x10 )` an error rather than 16. Stopping at the first thing it does not understand and reporting the value it happened to have is how a calculator silently answers the wrong question.

author: blu
body: The form a caller with no last-result wants. `$` in this one is an error rather than zero, because a caller that never supplied a previous value has none to give and should not be handed one.
